author: Scranton Reporter
title: Bresnahan visits Pittston food bank and donates food with staff
text:
U.S. Representative Rob Bresnahan, Jr. (PA-08) visited the Weinberg Northeast Regional Food Bank in Pittston over the weekend to support local families and observe the organization’s work. During his visit, Bresnahan and his staff donated food and volunteered by packing boxes for families in need.
“It doesn’t matter if Washington is open or not: our neighbors still need support,” said Rep. Bresnahan. “I’m proud of our team for showing up, and I’m grateful to Weinberg’s dedicated staff and volunteers for their tireless commitment to serving our communities. Especially during times of uncertainty, it’s our shared effort that keeps families fed.”
The Weinberg Northeast Regional Food Bank serves thousands of residents in Luzerne, Lackawanna, Susquehanna, and Wyoming Counties each year by distributing millions of pounds of food.
Earlier this year, Rep. Bresnahan introduced the Local Farmers Feeding our Communities Act. The legislation is endorsed by Feeding America and would allow states to use USDA cooperative agreements to connect local food distribution organizations with farmers and producers. Funds from these agreements would be used to buy local foods such as seafood, meat, milk, cheese, eggs, fruit, and poultry. The bill also allocates a portion of funds specifically for purchases from small, mid-size, beginning, and veteran farmers.
